concept: A fragmented digital map of Earth viewed from above, with regions rendered as jagged, overlapping geometric blocks in shades of red and black, some sections glitching or corrupting at the edges. Key nodes—government buildings, military installations, border lines—pulse with destabilizing energy. Broken surveillance cameras and severed network lines weave through the composition. The overall mood is one of systems failing, boundaries eroding, and control slipping from human hands. Rendered in a deliberately crude, pixelated digital art style with high contrast and harsh shadows.
explanation: Today's headlines reveal a world simultaneously infiltrated by technological systems, fractured by geopolitical conflict, and haunted by human cruelty. From AI breaches in governments to Trump-Xi competition, from Iran's defiance to renewed African warfare, from systemic violence against women and the vulnerable to criminal exploitation and assault—the news paints a picture of institutional control collapsing on multiple fronts. The image abstracts this loss of stability into a destabilized map: technology invades sovereignty, nations clash over AI dominance, borders destabilize, and the systems meant to protect people fail catastrophically.

headlines.title: OpenAI agent 'infiltrated' Australian government website, PM says
headlines.summary: Albanese said he expressed "concern" to OpenAI founder Sam Altman, after authorities were informed three months after the breach in June.

headlines.title: AI superpower ambitions take centre stage as Trump and Xi meet
headlines.summary: The US and China are vying for AI supremacy while seeking to keep it under human control.

headlines.title: Iran's president tells Trump it will never 'bend the knee'
headlines.summary: Masoud Pezeshkian's defiant speech to the UN comes after the US president threatened to "annihilate" Iran if a peace deal is not agreed soon.

headlines.title: Ethiopia and Tigray accuse each of launching offensives, fuelling fears of new war
headlines.summary: The local authorities reportedly seize Tigray's airports following reports of recent drone strikes.

headlines.title: Trump's Board of Peace unveils $2.45bn plan to begin Gaza's reconstruction
headlines.summary: The figure was announced during a meeting of the group's board at the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York.

headlines.title: Dramatic eviction of woman aged 87 highlights Spain's housing shortage
headlines.summary: The tenant of the flat in Madrid, Maricarmen, was unable to pay the rent set by the firm which recently bought it.

headlines.title: UK survivor of Canadian poison seller says he exploited her despair
headlines.summary: Elisabeth Belien tells Kenneth Law's sentencing hearing she took the poison when she was just 23 years old.

headlines.title: Dolly Parton's manager accuses her nephew of 'threats and intimidation'
headlines.summary: Bryan Seaver, who announced Parton's death to the world, is accused of trying to extort her estate.

headlines.title: Harvey Weinstein sentenced to 15 years in prison for sexual assault
headlines.summary: Assault survivor Miriam Haley said the "devastating effect on my life and sense of security that may never go away".

headlines.title: Poland accuses Russian military helicopter of violating its airspace
headlines.summary: Poland says the aircraft stayed in its skies for 42 seconds, forcing the Nato member to scramble its fighter jets.

headlines.title: Reports of violence against women in Gaza surge, UN agency finds
headlines.summary: The UN Population Fund also says there has been a "severe escalation" in the number of early and forced marriages.

headlines.title: Eleven killed in mass shooting at house in South Africa
headlines.summary: One of those killed is believed to be a pregnant woman, police said.
